title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Sister Sadie & the Kittredge Arts Center Grand Reopening
location: Kittredge Arts Center, Kittredge Theater
description:
On Friday October 2nd at 7 PM, Warren Wilson College celebrates the grand reopening of Kittredge Arts Center, with renowned Bluegrass act Sister Sadie headlining!  The Kittredge Arts Center grand reopening is part of the Warren Wilson College's 2026 Homecoming, and is also a homecoming for Sister Sadie's mandolinist, WWC alum' Rainy Miatke (Music Major, Class of 2025). 

 

Doors open at 6:15 PM with light refreshments, and concert starts at 7 PM.  

 

 

Tickets can be purchased here:  https://wwc-ventures.ticketspice.com/sister-sadie-and-the-kittredge-arts-center-grand-reopening 

 

For more information abuot the event, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916.  

 

 

Sister Sadie Bio:

What started as an accidental band became a force. GRAMMY-nominated. IBMA-decorated. Opry-validated. But for all the
accolades, they were often reduced to one line: an all-female bluegrass band. True—but never the point. Sister Sadie has always
been about the music. The fire. The truth.


Their new album, All Will Be Well, is that truth—loud, fearless, and free. You’ll hear echoes of bluegrass, but what rises is
something bigger: country with claws, Americana with muscle, gospel grit and raw storytelling.


From the haunting “Prodigal Daughter” to the swagger of “Do What You Want” and the aching beauty of “If I Don’t Have You,”
these six women are not performing roles—they’re telling you who they are.


This is Sister Sadie, evolved: bold, bonded, and braver than ever. They're not asking for space. They're taking it.


And they’re just getting started.

 

About Kittredge Arts Center:

Nestled within the beautiful, historic Warren Wilson College campus, the Kittredge Arts Center provides a centralized location for the arts at WWC and WNC. The Center features the 321-seat Kittredge Theater and 80-seat Williams Recital Hall, where music and performance events are featured throughout the year. Kittredge Arts Center is also available as a rental space to organizations looking for an affordable option in a beautiful location for conferences, business retreats, and other events. 

 

For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro (Assistant Professor of Music, Music Department Chair, and Director of Kittredge Arts Center) at 828-545-3916 or jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu

title: COMING FRIDAY OCTOBER 9th | Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue w/ Abraham Alexander
location: Sierra Nevada Mills River, 100 Sierra Nevada Way, Mills River, NC, 28732
description:
Friday, October 9 | Amphitheater Stage | 6 PM DOORS | 7PM SHOW | From $51.50 Event Details and Tickets 
Few artists embody the heart and soul of their city like Trombone Shorty. Perhaps the most recognizable ambassador for New Orleans music working today, Shorty has spent his entire life not only carrying the torch for Crescent City culture, but also propelling it forward into the 21st century with his ecstatic live performances and intoxicating blend of rock, funk, soul, jazz, blues, hip-hop, and Caribbean influences. 
On top of his relentless touring schedule, Shorty also managed to launch The Trombone Shorty Foundation in 2011, which supports youth music education in New Orleans and beyond. 
Academy Award® nominated artist Abraham Alexander is a rising singer songwriter whose soulful fusion of blues, folk, and gospel has captivated audiences around the world. Born in Athens, Greece to Nigerian parents and raised in Fort Worth, Texas, Alexander turned to music following a career ending soccer injury and personal tragedy. He released his breakout self-titled EP in 2019, earning attention for his emotional storytelling and powerful vocal presence. With his powerful presence and genre-defying sound, he continues to emerge as one of the most vital and visionary voices in contemporary music. 
Sierra Nevada Brewing Co. is one of America’s premier craft breweries, highly regarded for using only the finest quality ingredients.  Sierra Nevada has set the standard for craft brewers worldwide with innovations in the brewhouse as well as advances in sustainability. title: COMING SATURDAY OCTOBER 17th | The Infamous Stringdusters w/sg Broken Compass Bluegrass
location: Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain, 2948 US-70, Black Mountain, NC, 28711
description:
Saturday, October 17 | Doors: 6 pm | Show: 7:30 pm | From $36.30 Event Details and Tickets

celebrate 20 years since their inception, the ground-breaking, Grammy Award-winning ensemble The Infamous Stringdusters—whose tone and swagger meld acoustic majesty with the energy of a full-blown rock show—mark this milestone with the release of 20/20.
Twenty brand new songs, born from endless miles in pursuit of a dream. Formed in Nashville in the early 2000s while performing as side-men with stalwarts of the bluegrass community, the band members soaked up every influence like musical sponges. Their friendships, paired with a shared drive to create their own music and master their own destiny, inevitably led to the birth of The Infamous Stringdusters.
Alongside Chris Pandolfi (banjo), Travis Book (double bass), Jeremy Garrett (fiddle), Andy Hall (dobro), and Andy Falco (guitar), the group continues to fearlessly blur the boundaries between bluegrass, Americana, country, and indie-folk.

At its core, 20/20 represents a defining chapter for the Stringdusters, who embody sonic exploration and boundless curiosity while holding fast to musical tradition—whether under the bright stage lights or deep within the studio.

Pisgah Brewing Company currently operates the new indoor taproom with live music several days a week, plus our outdoor music venue in the summer and fall months with live music frequently on WNC’s premier outdoor music venue, the Pisgah Brewing Outdoor Stage. title: Bonsai in a Day: Learn, Create, Take Home
description:
Bonsai in a Day: Learn, Create, Take Home
with Rebecca Ayres 
Saturday, October 3  |  9:30 am – 4:30pm 
Register Here!
  
Although it has its roots in ancient Asian traditions, the living art of bonsai now enjoys enthusiasts throughout much of the world. This class will provide the basic concepts and skills for novices to begin growing and shaping their own miniature trees. The first half of the class will cover the fundamental horticultural and aesthetic principles of bonsai. It will include such topics as tree selection, watering, pest control, pruning, wiring, and styling. In the second half of the class, each participant will receive a pot, scissors, wire, and planting medium. With guidance from the instructor, the students will create their own bonsai to take home. Materials included in registration. 
Rebecca Ayres is a ceramic artist and gardener. A longtime Arboretum volunteer, she is the assistant to the bonsai curator and helps with overseeing the exhibition garden, the collection and the Carolina Bonsai Expo. She is a member of the Blue Ridge Bonsai Society, where she has taught workshops and classes, and is a graduate of the Arboretum’s Blue Ridge Naturalist program.

If you are unfamiliar with the Camino, here are a few links to learn more:

\*[American Pilgrims on the Camino](https://americanpilgrims.org/iwpmap_directory/western-north-carolina/)

* [Stingy Nomads Camino](https://stingynomads.com/camino-de-santiago-walking-guide/)
\*[Gronze Camino Planner](https://www.gronze.com/)
* [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_(2010_film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_(2010_film))

**Distance:** 5, 7, or 11 miles
**Pace: 3.2 mph**

**Start Times**
**9:30 am**\- Meet at First Congregational Church\, 1735 5th Ave W\, Hendersonville\, NC
**11:15 - 11:45 - Southern Streams coffee across from the FCC church.**

First Section: The first section is a five mile loop. The loop ends at Southern Streams coffee house, which is across from the church where we start. Join us here for coffee, even if you don't have time to walk.

Second Section: Starting at about 11:45 am from Southern Streams coffee, continue through lower Laurel Park. For those who want to exit, you can return to the church on the Ecusta Trail for a total of about 7 miles.

Last Section: To downtown and St. James Church, returning via Ecusta Trail. 10.5 miles total distance.
The church historian will be on hand to give a brief history of the stained glass windows in the church. And we will have cake.

**Caution:** There are a few stretches on busy roads where we will need to walk single file.

Full Route: [Laurel Park Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/laurel-park-loop-improved-3937230?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)

Parking: We are meeting at the First Congregational Church. Please carpool if possible.

Dogs: On leash the entire time. The first section is shady, but the pavement may be hot on the last section. Please consider your pup's feet in the heat.

Scenic Asheville Series: This hike counts as a Wildcard substitute on my Scenic Asheville Series. There are 9 [hikes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11ewlUM9OV8I4npc1cNNsSYOnXI0QPw2isAleXdFzEbI/edit?usp=drivesdk) in the series; hike them all and receive an [attractive badge](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit) for your backpack. Check your status [HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk/edit?gid=0#gid=0).

**Questions**
If you have questions, call the hike leader (Gracen) at 828-290-0886.

**Guests:** For this hike, there are no guest restrictions. Bring them with you.

title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. 
The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibitions. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. 
Join Joshua on October 3, November 7, and December 5. 
ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST
Joshua Canter is a mindfulness meditation teacher and the founder of True Nature Travels and Education, an Asheville-based organization that has offered transformative retreats and educational experiences around the world for more than 20 years. He holds a master’s degree in Contemplative Psychology and is passionate about making mindfulness accessible, grounded, and relevant to everyday life.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: *Cancelled* Adult Studio: Beginner Drop Spinning
location: NC
description:
Your life is filled with textiles made from various spun threads and yarn. Come deepen those connections with the fibers that are deeply woven into many aspects of our lives by trying your hand at one of the earliest ways to handspin yarn using a drop spindle. 
Join us for a fun, educational and meditative day of learning the top whirl dropspindle, and maybe some other styles as well. We will prepare, card and spin raw wool fleece to create yarn on a drop spindle. You may have time to try different types of fibers and even different types of spindles. You will get to take home your first handspun yarn, as well as a drop spindle to continue exploring this new skill. 
ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST
Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with more than 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the Southeastern United States, including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils.  Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.

title: Naturalist Walk and Talk - Spiders
description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk – Spiders
with Shane Myers 
Saturday, October 3  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. 
This month we will focus on the Spiders of the Arboretum. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall
description:
Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall
with Asheville Wellness Tours 
Saturday, October 3  |  2 – 5pm 
Register Here!
  
Join us for a celebration of autumn delights during this restorative afternoon nature connection retreat! From fall foliage to the monarch migration, we will immerse ourselves in the kaleidoscope that is autumn in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Enlivening our senses, calming our weary minds, and lingering in liminality. Together, we will discover natural pathways to equilibrium that will help us navigate life’s ups and downs, as well as the upcoming holiday season. 
Your guide, Kelly Bruce, will lead you on a colorful journey through the fall forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative afternoon on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience in community, enjoying a special wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Kelly Bruce is a writer, forest therapy guide and nature connection mentor based in Hendersonville, North Carolina. Her mission is to help others deepen their connection with nature, community and Self. Kelly is an Association of Nature and Forest Therapy Certified Guide and Certification Consultant. She is Wilderness First Aid and CPR certified by the American Red Cross.

The original music of Jake Salter & a unique group of talented musicians come together in Tru Phonic. Sounds of Jam, Funk, Blues, Rock, Soul, Jazz and Hip-Hop & more can be heard when seeing the band Live or on their Studio Albums. Established in 2017, Tru Phonic includes Multiple veterans in the Central Florida music scene who have worked with many other great bands and musicians in the area. The group has an ever-changing, high-energy live show that makes you wanna MOVE! Tru Phonic’s original sound is characterized by high skill-level shown on each instrument, talented vocal harmonies, powerful lyrics, expanding grooves, unique guitar playing & a tight horn section.   
​In just a few years of touring Tru Phonic has made quite an impression everywhere they go, establishing fanbases & regular listeners in cities allover the Southeast U.S. & Booking Music Festivals Like Suwannee Hulaween 2023, Farm to Grass, Whippersnap Music & arts Fest, Sunshine Hootenany, Everglades Roots Fest, No Resolutions, Fort20 Fest & more…. 
The band also has a strong online presence & following with their original music accumulating steady numbers in just over 6 years; 
-over 230,000 streams across all platforms

title: Millpond Connector at Haywood Community College on National Taco Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
As we enter Leaf Season, the temperature may indeed be cooler. Let's celebrate by going out for tacos after the walk.

To get to the Millpond Connector from our start point, we will go clockwise on the Bobcat Trail and then take the Kingfisher Trail to the Copperhead Trail. When we intersect with the Millpond Connector, we will turn left, finishing the campus loop on the Bobcat Trail. Altogether, it isn't over 2 miles. Part of the walk is on pavement, part on well-groomed trail, and part on not-as-well groomed trail. There is some small elevation change.

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring one walking stick, just in case. As always, you are urged to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have any problem. There are no bathrooms available on a Sunday afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles!

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: AYPROS Government Relations Crew: October Meeting with Mayoral Candidates
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
Local government decisions shape nearly every part of life in Asheville, from housing and transportation to economic development, public safety, parks, and the future of downtown. Understanding how those decisions are made, and where residents can have a meaningful voice, is not always as straightforward.

Join the AYPROS Government Relations Crew for our October meeting as we continue creating a place where young professionals can better understand local government, discuss the issues affecting our region, and become more informed and involved in the future of Asheville and Buncombe County.

This month, we are pleased to welcome **Asheville City Mayor Esther Manheimer and City Councilor and Mayoral Candidate Kim Roney.**

Members will have an opportunity to hear directly from both, ask questions, and contribute their own perspectives to the conversation.

## What You Can Expect

Each month, the Government Relations Crew gathers for a focused, working-style discussion covering current issues affecting Asheville and Buncombe County.

Throughout the year, Crew members will also have opportunities to:

* Hear from community leaders, elected officials, planners, and policy experts
* Attend City Council and other public meetings together
* Organize around initiatives that align with AYPROS’ mission
* Take field visits to better understand projects and community issues firsthand
* Help continue building programs such as 828 Lead, 828 Vote, and AYPROS Day at the Capitol

Our goal is not to advocate from assumptions. It is to become informed, thoughtful leaders who can positively influence our community.

## Who Should Attend

The Government Relations Crew is open to any AYPROS member who wants to better understand local government, public policy, and the issues affecting our community.
Whether you are already civically engaged, work in a related field, or are simply curious about how decisions get made, you are welcome to join us. No prior experience is required, and first-time attendees are encouraged to participate.

## Calling All 828 Lead Graduates

Bring your **828 Lead binder**, wear your **828 Lead pin** if you have one, and represent your cohort. This is a chance to put what you learned into practice and continue building your understanding of local leadership and government.

## Event Details

**Monday, September 14, 2026**
**9:00 AM - 10:00 AM**

Hatchworks Coworking
45 S. French Broad Avenue, Suite 170
Asheville, NC 28801

If you are interested in helping shape the future of Asheville while spending time with other engaged young professionals, we would be glad to have you join us.

Please register so we know you are coming.

Coffee will be provided!

description:
Hendo Fun Friends
Darlene will host a hike on the Pilot Cove/Slate Rock Loop in Pisgah Forest;
Hidden deep within the Mills River area of Pisgah National Forest, this trail has rhododendrons and Mtn laurel. And, at the top, there is a great view from the Forked Ridge Pluton. Probably the BEST Fall color view.

**IF YOU HAVE AN ORANGE VEST; WEAR IT. HUNTING SEASON HAS STARTED. ;-) THEY ARE INEXPENSIVE AT WALMART....**
We are the ***HFF Trail Trekkers***: We a’gonna get our step-counters a’workin’ !!

Pavel Wlosok brings his quartet to the corner for an evening of contemporary jazz played by musicians who have all, in their own ways, arrived in Asheville by circuitous routes. Pavel himself came from Ostrava via Texas, a Czech pianist who landed at the University of North Texas in 1995 with one backpack and has spent the decades since building one of the more quietly remarkable careers in American jazz. Expect originals alongside deep-catalog interpretations, the lyricism of Pavel's writing anchoring music that moves with the unhurried authority of players who trust one another and the form. title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, October 6  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Flat Creek Tr & BRPkwy, a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
I am going to the Flat Creek Tr on the Heintooga spur of the BRPkwy; and **return on the BRPkwy.** Up to 12 of you are welcome to join me.
Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have pleasant surprises.
Flat Creek Trail is an amazingly beautiful 2.7 mile 1-way hike located just off The Blue Ridge Parkway, in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park. The trail follows alongside two different creeks, and is full of lush moss, grass and trees making for an absolutely gorgeous and beautiful hike that begins at the Heintooga Picnic area
Woodlands of red spruce, American beech, yellow birch, and striped and red maple make this trail a real treat.
A bull elk and his family are known to be in this area. We saw them last time!
**WE WILL RETURN VIA THE BRPKWY** with a few overlook stops. (rest stop at Waterrock Knob).
Difficulty: 5 (easy) rockhop Crk Xings. Short steep section at the end.
**This event requires a car shuttle. Sedans acceptable.**
John Muir didn’t like the word ‘hike’. “We ought to saunter through them reverently, not 'hike' through them.”
We are the **Sloth Hike Team of WNC**: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t ***!!***
**Hike Details:**
(Social ‘hour’ at 9 AM. Parade leaves at 9:10a)
Length: 3.0 mi total; Total **descent**: 800 ft: Accum ascent: 400 ft; Elevation: 5000ft
Pace: **1.5mph**
**We eat, snack & drink ‘on the go’.**
Drive time: 60mi/1.75hr (1-way) from Brevard; via Hwy 276 thru Maggie Valley.
**Return trip drive time:** via BRPkwy/Hwy 215: 85 mi/2.25hrs
**Return Not earlier than: 4:30PM (=7.5 hrs)**
Trailhead: Google Map = “Heintooga Overlook”
Carpool contributions appreciated. $12.00 suggested (includes parking pass fee)
**THIS IS NOT A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** we will be in the GSMNP.
Weather Check: Waynesville, NC

I currently have 1 driver(s). (=??ppl)

Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
We suggest masks and open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.

title: AYPROS All Access 2026
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
What would you ask someone who is exactly as successful right now as you hope to be someday?

How did you start? What was your biggest failure? What do you wish you knew at 25 or 30? What decision changed everything? And what would you tell someone sitting where you are right now?
**AYPROS All Access** is built around those conversations.

On **Tuesday, October 6**, a small group of Asheville’s young professionals will sit at the table with eight accomplished founders, executives and community leaders for an evening unlike anything we have done before.
This is not a panel. There is no keynote. You will not spend the night sitting in rows listening to someone speak from a stage.

Instead, attendees will take part in **four 20-minute small-group conversations**, rotating from table to table throughout the evening. Each table will be hosted by one of our featured leaders, giving you the chance to ask questions, hear the stories behind their successes and failures, and have the kind of conversation most people rarely get access to.

### Your All Access Table Leaders

**Barry E.A. Johnson**
Former Obama Administration official, founding Executive Director of SelectUSA, and longtime business and economic development leader.

**Chris Heivly**
Co-founder of MapQuest, entrepreneur, investor and former Managing Director of Techstars.

**Amy Daniels**
Executive Director of the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation and longtime nonprofit and philanthropic leader.

**Dr. Richard Furman**
Surgeon, entrepreneur and co-founder of World Medical Mission.

**Michael Ciochetti**
Entrepreneur and developer behind one of the country’s most celebrated private fly-in communities.

**Rachel Sossoman**
Healthcare executive and leader in Western North Carolina.

**Vic Isley**
President & CEO of Explore Asheville and a nationally recognized tourism and destination leader.

**Kwame Anku**
Founder, investor and entrepreneur working with companies and founders across the country.

After the four conversations, the evening opens up for drinks, food and time to continue the conversations that started around the tables.
All Access is intentionally limited. The point is not to fill a ballroom. It is to create a room where you can actually **sit across from people you admire, ask the questions you have always wanted to ask, and leave knowing people you probably would not have known otherwise.**

One evening.
Eight leaders.
Four conversations.
A seat at the table.

**Tuesday, October 6, 2026**
**Asheville, NC**
Attendance is limited.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**October 2026 Selection - *Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead* by Olga Tokarczuk**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Drive-Your-Plow-Over-Bones/dp/0525541330/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/51648276-drive-your-plow-over-the-bones-of-the-dead)

*In a remote Polish village, Janina devotes the dark winter days to studying astrology, translating the poetry of William Blake, and taking care of the summer homes of wealthy Warsaw residents. Her reputation as a crank and a recluse is amplified by her not-so-secret preference for the company of animals over humans. Then a neighbor, Big Foot, turns up dead. Soon other bodies are discovered, in increasingly strange circumstances. As suspicions mount, Janina inserts herself into the investigation, certain that she knows whodunit. If only anyone would pay her mind . . .*

*A deeply satisfying thriller cum fairy tale, Drive Your Plow over the Bones of the Dead is a provocative exploration of the murky borderland between sanity and madness, justice and tradition, autonomy and fate. Whom do we deem sane? it asks. Who is worthy of a voice?*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: In Conversation | An Artist Talk by Lesley Dill
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for an evening with New York-based artist Lesley Dill, whose work is featured in the current exhibition, The Art of Paper. Dill will talk about her projects that involve paper and collaboration, from huge community and large-scale installations to the intimate creation of artist books and sculptures, as well as her work with artists, poets, students, and studios, such as Tamarind and Dieu Donne.  
PAPER IS MY FRIEND:  
“Paper is about fingertip energy for me. The way one moves in to touch paper is like no other approach. It’s as if each finger has a little imaginary rocketship in it. We touch nothing else the way we touch paper. Paper is the medium of intimacy. The end result is wonder. All printmaking begins with the choice of what paper and in this way, it is about a relationship to fragility and force. This relationship comes from Poetry.”  
ABOUT THE ARTIST
Lesley Dill is an American artist working at the intersection of language and fine art in sculpture, printmaking, installation and performance, exploring the power of words to cloak and reveal the psyche. Dill has had over one hundred solo exhibitions. Her artworks are in the collections of many major museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Museum of Modern Art, New York. In 2017 she was named a fellow of The John Simon Guggenheim Foundation. Her opera, Divide Light, based on the poems of Emily Dickinson, was performed in San Jose in 2008, restaged in New York City in 2018, and captured in an award-winning film by Ed Robbins. Dill’s exhibition Wild Grace This Private Hallucinatory Moment at Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans (2025–26), a result of research conducted as a 2023–2024 Smithsonian Artist Research Fellow, examined themes of radiance and healing in seen and unseen energies. Dill’s exhibition Wilderness: Light Sizzles Around Me, organized by the Figge Art Museum and traveled to seven venues from 2021 to 2023, amplifies voices of the North American past as they wrestle with divinity, deviltry, and freedom, including Mother Ann Lee, Black Hawk, Sojourner Truth, John Brown, Emily Dickinson, Horace Pippin, and Sister Gertrude Morgan. Ms. Dill is represented by Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans. She lives and works in Brooklyn, New York. For more information and images of her work, visit www.lesleydill.net

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

Wednesday, October 7  |  10am – 12pm

Do you want to learn to take better seasonal fall photos in the gardens? Join us for a hands-on workshop where we use whatever camera you are working with to learn tips, tricks, and techniques to take the photos you are hoping to capture. Bring your phone, a point and shoot camera, digital SLR or film SLR camera. This class is for all levels of photographers.

title: Weave Kudzu Vines Into a Basket
description:
Weave Kudzu Vines Into a Basket
with Carleigh Fairchild 
Wednesday, October 7  |  10am – 4pm 
Register Here!
  
Turn wild vines into a basket in this hands-on kudzu weaving workshop. Kudzu, often thought of as an invasive plant, offers a surprising gift: strong, flexible vines that make for beautiful, functional baskets. In this workshop you’ll learn how to identify, harvest, and prepare kudzu responsibly, turning an abundant wild plant into a useful basket. Together we’ll explore weaving techniques and create baskets that reflect each of our creativity. Come away with your own handmade basket, practical knowledge for future projects, and a new appreciation for kudzu. There will be a 30 minute lunch break and materials will be provided. If you have sharp pruners, feel free to bring them along! 
Carleigh Fairchild has a deep love for the Earth. She gardens, keeps bees, wild harvests, processes animals, tans hides, weaves baskets, and finds joy in time spent around the fire. As the founder of Human Nature Connection LLC, she is dedicated to helping others rediscover respectful and collaborative relationships with the more then human world. Carleigh’s journey—including 86 days on the survival show ALONE in Patagonia—deepened her understanding of belonging and connection. With over 25 years of experience, she teaches both online and in-person classes in Western North Carolina, weaving together earth skills, community, and healing. Carleigh is also a NIASZIIH bodywork healer and instructor at Wilderness Fusion, integrating body, earth, and spirit in her practice.

title: The Big Asheville Science Salon!
description:
Welcome to the tremendous, amazing, Big Asheville Science Salon!
When the Weather Gets Weird with atmospheric scientist Dr. Douglas Miller. 
       All I’m saying is that the itsy-bitsy spider could’ve used a heads-up. 
We get alerts about price drops for kitchen appliances we never wanted, reminders to change our engine oil, and updates on celebrity meltdowns. We also get warnings when weather events might turn our whole world upside down (yes, we’re still talking about you, Helene), which is arguably a more useful predictive tool. Note: forecasting the path and magnitude of storms is no small feat, and we should be extremely grateful that some scientists consider weather more than just a topic for small talk. 
But what about the consequences of extreme weather (the “downstream effects”, so to speak)? Is it possible to predict, with any degree of accuracy, the likelihood that rainfall will lead to floods or landslides? Maybe, someone could start by examining rainfall patterns in the region, fluctuations in river and stream levels, and the growing number of documented landslides across our mountains. 
At the October salon, let’s talk about the weather – and how to develop a landslide watch and warning system – with atmospheric scientist Dr. Douglas Miller. Dr. Miller is a Professor in the Department of Atmospheric Sciences and a Distinguished Professor in Interdisciplinary Studies at UNC Asheville. His research focuses on how mountains affect weather and, specifically, their ability to amplify the impact of weather events. For more than two decades, Doug has pondered the puzzles of precipitation in western North Carolina, investigating connections between atmospheric rivers and landslides, rainfall variability, and how cold air damming (i.e., when mountains block air from the north and trap it as a cool air dome) creates unique weather patterns. 
Our mission: Cultivate curiosity and build community by sharing the coolest, grooviest, and fascinating-ist scientific discoveries. And have a beer (or wine or soda). 
How it do: Each month, a bona fide expert takes us on a thrill ride of science awesomeness (i.e., talk about their research and probably show pretty pictures). Afterwards, a lively Q&A segues into general mingling and chatting about why science is so cool. 
When: First Wednesday of each month. 
                Doors: 6:00pm; Presentation: 7:00pm; Socializing: 8:00pm 
Where: The Mule (at Devil’s Foot Beverage) 131 Sweeten Creek Rd., Asheville, NC 28803 
No cover charge – just bring your brain! 
Doors open at 5:00. Have a drink with old friends, meet new ones, and get ready for some serious science in a seriously un-serious setting.

title: The Polyvagal Sangha
description:
Inner Peace Collective
**The Polyvagal Sangha**
*A community of seekers exploring nervous system regulation through the lens of ancient wisdom and modern science.*

A new tribe is forming. We're inviting 30 like-minded and like-hearted folks into an ongoing inquiry — learning to cultivate a greater felt sense of calm, ease, safety, and resilience in our bodies, our relationships, and the world around us. The goal isn't just personal regulation, but a ripple effect of co-regulation: a shift in how we show up for others and move through our own lives.

This is the first class in a 3-class series. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts, yet a single dive will yield beneficial results towards salutogenesis.

**Teachers:** Omri Sitton, D.C. and Wills Reed, LCMHCA

**Cost:** $10–$15 suggested donation to local nonprofit *Source Of Wellness*.
\*No one is turned away for lack of funds — all donations are appreciated.

**How to Reserve Your Spot** (please do both — priority goes to folks who complete both steps):

1. **Text Omri at 828-298-0011** with your name and whether you'd like to pay via Venmo or at the door
2. **RSVP on Meetup** using the button on this page

*A note on the two-step process: based on past events, people who only RSVP on Meetup often don't show up. Texting Omri directly helps us plan for who's actually coming — so please do both.*

**A Bit More Detail:**
Polyvagal Theory (PVT) — conceptualized by Stephen Porges — reveals how our body and brain collaborate to respond to everyday stress and deeply held trauma. It highlights the role of the autonomic nervous system, especially the vagus nerve, in shaping our physical and mental health. Paired with mindfulness practices drawn from ancient traditions, PVT offers us both the science and the felt experience of coming back to our center.

By building community together, we naturally stimulate the social engagement system — the nervous system's highest branch — fostering connection, safety, and ease in body, mind, and life. This is the essence of The Polyvagal Sangha.

**Participants will learn:**

* Polyvagal Theory's three defining principles
* Somatic activities specific to each branch of the autonomic nervous system
* Awareness practices to soften emotional triggers and past traumas
* The body's innate biological responses, and the role of mindfulness in being present to "what is"
* How connecting with others committed to personal growth naturally lifts and supports us all

Join Omri and Wills for a series of illustrated, experiential presentations that will inspire your spirit, engage your mind, and challenge your creativity — as you uncover the enormous potential of applying this work in your daily life.

*Feel Well. Heal Well. Live Well.*

**About the teachers:**

**About Omri**
Omri Sitton, D.C., Cert. ZB has 25 years of experience in multiple fields of the healing arts. His passion in helping others has a strong emphasis on self-care.

He naturally weaves the connection between mindfulness practice, cellular consciousness, and polyvagal theory into his experiential classes.

Dr. Omri practices Tonal Chiropractic, Zero Balancing, and Polyvagal Touch in Asheville, offering what he refers to as ChiroSomatics.
Learn more at [omsourcewellness.com](https://www.omsourcewellness.com/)

**About Wills**
Wills Reed, LCMHCA, is an Asheville-based psychotherapist with a particular interest in how our earliest relationships, life experiences, and nervous systems shape the way we experience ourselves and others.

His work draws from attachment-focused therapy, EMDR, somatic approaches, and a longtime personal practice of meditation and contemplative traditions. He enjoys helping people translate these ideas into practical experiences of greater safety, connection, and freedom in everyday life.

title: Trembling, Still: The Awful Clarity of a Mind in Eclipse
location: Kittredge Arts Center, Kittredge Theater
description:
Time & Location

Oct 07, 2026, 7:00 PM – 9:30 PM

Kittredge Theatre, Warren Wilson College, 701 Warren Wilson Rd, Swannanoa, NC 28778, USA

About the Event

RSVP HERE

An evening with Stephen Jenkinson and Kimberly Ann Johnson

Hosted by Aditi Sethi

 

Wednesday, October 7, 2026 

7:00 to 9:00 pm conversation

9:00 to 9:30 pm book signing

 

Some books are written from a distance. This one was not.

 

In January of 2024, Stephen Jenkinson received a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease and began keeping a journal. He had spent decades walking alongside dying people and their families, first as director of palliative care at a Toronto hospital and later through the Orphan Wisdom School. Now the country he had guided so many others through had arrived at his own door.

 

What he wrote across that first year became Trembling, Still: The Awful Clarity of a Mind in Eclipse. It is a dated chronicle rather than a memoir, written in real time, with no benefit of hindsight and no idea yet how the year would end. He has said that he did not so much write the book as panic it onto the page, and that he had to invent words to carry what the ordinary ones could not. There is a glossary of them in the back. What began in devastation opened, unexpectedly, into mystery, and into a kind of mercy that did not depend on hope.

 

Much of it was written while Stephen was staying with Kimberly Ann Johnson, his friend and the co-author of Reckoning. On the evening of October 7 they step back into that time in person, on stage, here in Swannanoa.

 

The evening is a conversation between the two of them. Aditi Sethi, hospice physician and Emberlight's founder, will welcome Stephen and Kimberly to the stage, open the evening, and hold its shape. Then Stephen and Kimberly take the conversation from there, in front of us, for two hours. Afterward they will be signing books and available for brief exchanges.

 

They will talk about the experience around making this book, and how it has evolved since it was captured on the page in that moment in time. What was happening in the rooms around the writing, and what did not make it onto the page. What has held true in the two years since, and what has quietly fallen away. They will look at that season from where they stand now, and let us listen in.

 

At Emberlight, we practice ways to embrace death and support one another with loving presence. Deep listening, compassion, and bearing witness are how we meet people at the bedside, and they are what this evening asks of all of us in the room. This is not a lecture about mortality. It is a chance to sit in the company of someone speaking plainly from inside his own undoing, alongside a friend who was there for the writing of it, and to let that honesty do what honesty does.

 

You can purchase a copy of Trembling, Still online here if you would like to read ahead, and bring it with you to be signed. Stephen and Kimberly will also have copies available at the event.

 

Where and when

We gather at the Kittredge Theatre in the Kittredge Arts Center at Warren Wilson College,

701 Warren Wilson Rd, Swannanoa, NC 28778.

 

Doors open at 6:30 pm. The conversation runs from 7:00 to 9:00 pm, followed by the book signing until 9:30 pm.

 

About Stephen Jenkinson

Stephen Jenkinson is a culture activist and ceremony man, a practitioner of the eloquence of tongue and hand. He is an author, storyteller, musician, sculptor, raconteur, and off grid organic farmer, and has published seven books over a public life spent advocating for conscious living and dying. He worked extensively with dying people and their families, formerly serving as director of palliative care at Mount Sinai Hospital of Toronto. He is the creator of the Orphan Wisdom School, cofounded with his wife Nathalie Roy in 2010, and co-founder of the Nights of Grief and Mystery with singer songwriter Gregory Hoskins. He holds a master's degree in theology from Harvard University and a master's of social work from the University of Toronto. In 2023 Harvard honored him with a Distinguished Alumni Award for helping people navigate grief and connecting humanity through ceremony and storytelling. He is the subject of the documentary Griefwalker, and author of the award winning Die Wise.

 

About Kimberly Ann Johnson

Kimberly Ann Johnson is a somatic practitioner, postpartum advocate, and culture worker. She studied yoga directly with the three main lineage holders of the Krishnamacharya tradition and taught for fifteen years while running a Structural Integration practice. When her life was rearranged by childbirth, she turned toward the cultural chasm around postpartum care and trained in Somatic Experiencing and Sexological Bodywork to support women through birth injury, gynecological surgery, and sexual boundary violation. She is the author of Call of the Wild and the early mothering classic The Fourth Trimester, and co-authored Reckoning with Stephen Jenkinson. Her next book, Erotic Seasons: Tuning into the Rhythms of Women's Sexuality and Spirituality, arrives in November from St. Martin's Press. She hosts the Sex Birth Trauma podcast and is the steward of Mothering the Bones.

 

About Aditi Sethi, MD

Dr. Aditi Sethi is a hospice and palliative care physician, end of life doula, musician, and the founder and Executive Director of Emberlight: Center for Conscious Living & Dying. Her accompaniment of Ethan Sisser in the final weeks of his life is documented in the film The Last Ecstatic Days, and the question Ethan asked her then, whether dying might be a communal experience rather than a solitary one, became the seed of this organization. She is an emerging and important voice for shifting our culture's approach to dying, death, and grief tending.

 

 

 

 

This is a Pay What You Can event, and all proceeds support Emberlight. The care we offer is free to every resident and family who comes to us, and it stays free because this community holds it up. Your ticket goes directly into that work. We invite you to give what feels right for you, and if you are able to give beyond the suggested amount, that generosity is what keeps a bed open and a hand held for the next person who needs one. We would love to welcome you into this circle whatever the amount.

 

Please note that all event tickets are non-refundable, except in the case that Emberlight cancels the event.

 

Please contact events@emberlightway.org with any questions.

title: AYPROS Mug Club: FLOUR
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
### **NEW TIME: 8:30–10:00 AM**

Start your Thursday with AYPROS at Flour in downtown Asheville.
If Pub Club is your after-work hangout, Mug Club is the morning version. Coffee instead of cocktails, a little caffeine before the workday, and the same easy chance to catch up with familiar faces and meet other young professionals from across Asheville.

##### **And heads up: Mug Club is starting a little later! Beginning this month, we’re moving from 8:00–10:00 AM to 8:30–10:00 AM.**

For October, we’re headed downtown to Flour, a locally owned café on Wall Street serving coffee alongside scratch-made breakfast, biscuits and fresh-baked pastries. Come for the coffee, stay for the company, and maybe let a biscuit talk you into breakfast.

Mug Club is intentionally casual. Leave your business cards at home, come as you are, grab a coffee and settle in for a little while. No program. No presentations. No awkward agenda. Just good coffee and good people before the workday gets going.

Coming by yourself? Perfectly normal. Haven’t been to an AYPROS event before? Even better. Mug Club is one of the easiest ways to show up, meet a few people and see what AYPROS is all about.

**Your first drip coffee is on us.** Specialty drinks, additional coffee and other menu items will be available for purchase.

This is a come-and-go event, so arrive when you can and stay as long as your morning allows.

## What to Expect

* A relaxed morning at Flour in downtown Asheville
* Your first drip coffee on us
* Specialty drinks, breakfast and other menu items available for purchase
* Plenty of time to catch up with friends and meet new people
* No formal program, presentations or agenda
* Come by yourself, bring a friend or invite a coworker
* Come when you can and head out whenever you need to

**Flour**
40 Wall Street
Asheville, NC 28801

**Parking:** Downtown street and garage parking is available nearby, including the Wall Street Garage at 45 Wall Street.

title: The Art of Bonsai: Cultivating Your Appreciation
description:
The Art of Bonsai: Cultivating Your Appreciation
with Rebecca Ayres 
Thursday, October 8  |  1 – 2:30pm 
Register Here!
  
Do you enjoy visiting the bonsai collection at the Arboretum but wish you had a deeper understanding of the art of bonsai? If you’d like to learn more about the cultivation and shaping of bonsai, but don’t necessarily want grow your own, this class is for you. It will cover the history of bonsai from ancient China to the Arboretum’s Bonsai Exhibition Garden. It will show the aesthetic qualities that are desirable in bonsai. While this course doesn’t cover all the detailed information you’d want for growing your own little trees, it does discuss how bonsai are started, nurtured, pruned, root-pruned, and wired. You’ll get behind-the-scenes views of the care of bonsai at the Arboretum and learn what makes the Arboretum’s bonsai display special. You’ll get some tips on where and when to see bonsai at the Arboretum and other public displays. 
Rebecca Ayres is a ceramic artist and gardener. A longtime Arboretum volunteer, she is the assistant to the bonsai curator and helps with overseeing the exhibition garden, the collection and the Carolina Bonsai Expo. She is a member of the Blue Ridge Bonsai Society, where she has taught workshops and classes, and is a graduate of the Arboretum’s Blue Ridge Naturalist program.

Thursday, October 8, 2026 from 6 to 8 p.m.
Blue Ridge Court at The North Carolina Arboretum

The North Carolina Arboretum and Chemist Spirits have come together to create a one-of-a-kind botanical vodka inspired by the plants and landscapes of Western North Carolina. Explore the flavors and botanicals behind the spirit before creating your own botanical-infused cocktail, guided by the experts who developed it. Then settle in and enjoy the evening with live music and heavy hors d’oeuvres in one of the Arboretum’s most beautiful settings. 
Each guest will also receive a commemorative 40th Anniversary Arboretum tasting glass to take home. Parking is included.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Bent Creek-Sidehill: 7 mi 1000 ft elev. gain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**[Sign-up opens Sunday, Oct. 4th, 8:00 pm]**

This is a "Todd Hike" that's mostly on Lower Sidehill Trail and South Ridge Rd. It's a pretty area deep into Bent Creek. The plan is for a "lollipop" with a short stem at the start and finish, and a big loop the rest of the way.

Be prepared for a moderate pace, around 2.4 mph. There's good footing throughout, with a combination of forest trails and gravel roads. Ups and downs are relatively mild. If you're on the fence about poles, you probably won't need them here. Bring water and, if you're inclined, a snack, too. There'll be a little break somewhere around the middle.

**CARPOOLING TIME & PLACE**

There's limited trailhead parking, so we'll carpool from the Asheville Outlets behind the Waffle House (directions below). Look for me and my silver Hyundai. Come early to allow for traffic. We'll depart by 9:00 AM

Here's the Waffle House location on Google Maps:
[https://goo.gl/maps/kjkQTmGQA7QNgbWLA](https://goo.gl/maps/kjkQTmGQA7QNgbWLA)

**From Exit 33 on I-26,**

* Head south a short distance on Brevard Rd. (Rt. 191) to the traffic light with Ingles on the right and Waffle House on the left.
* Turn Left into the Asheville Outlets.
* Drive just past the Waffle House and turn left onto the parking lot access road, NOT into the Waffle House lot.
* Take the first right. We'll park and meet in this area of the lot.

**ALSO IMPORTANT**
***Dogs.*** Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but U.S. Forest Service regulations require leashes. Wear sensible hiking boots. Bring some water. If you're on the fence about hiking poles, you probably don't need them for this one.

***Guests.*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they must join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike independently. Alternatively, contact me in advance to ask if it's okay to bring a +1 after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, we may be able to add your guest.

**COURTESY TO WAITLISTERS** (Please abide!)
Only sign up if you \*truly\* plan to come. And if you're on the borderline of dropping out for any reason, buck up and join us! I promise you'll be glad you did.

If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers can have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't ever be a "no-show" for any MeetUp events. Let your organizer know in advance.

If you're on the waiting list, keep checking the evening before. Despite what I wrote above, we usually have last-minute dropouts.

**WEATHER**
I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:30 AM if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-
**LEGALESE**
This Asheville Hiking Group (AHG) event involves hiking and, possibly, transportation to and from the meetup site. Participants are responsible for their own safety and affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Hiking may involve risks to oneself and property. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can assure your safety nor eliminate all risks. Participants assume full responsibility for any damages or losses.

title: Introduction to Permaculture Design
description:
Introduction to Permaculture Design
with Jennifer Verprauskus 
Friday, October 9  |  10 am – 1pm 
BREG – Core 
Register Here!
  
Permaculture is a design approach that works with nature rather than against it, creating landscapes that are productive, resilient, and regenerative. In this introductory workshop, participants will learn the foundational ethics and principles of permaculture and discover how thoughtful design can reduce maintenance, conserve resources, improve biodiversity, and create beautiful, functional outdoor spaces. 
Through discussion, examples, and hands-on exercises, attendees will explore how to observe natural patterns, understand site conditions, and apply simple design strategies to gardens, homesteads, and residential landscapes. Whether you are a homeowner, gardener, designer, or simply curious about sustainable living, this class provides practical tools for creating landscapes that thrive over time. 
Jennifer Verprauskus is a North Carolina Licensed Landscape Architect and a Permaculture Design Certificate Holder. She studied Landscape Architecture at the University of Massachusetts & Cal Poly. Since graduating, she has traveled the world to help people grow trees and their own food. She is the founder of both UpBeet Landscapes and BareRoot Designs, PLLC.

title: Fall Ecology Walk
description:
Fall Ecology Walk
with Dan Lazar 
Friday, October 9  |  1:30 – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Core 
Register Here!
  
Participants will walk through the garden and then head into the Arboretum Forest on easily accessible trails. Along the way we’ll take in autumn wildflowers and the changing hues on autumn’s rich palette of colors apparent on the diverse species of our native trees. We’ll learn how each autumn in Southern Appalachia is different, due in part to this biological diversity and changing climate conditions over the course of the year. 
This program takes place in the classroom and outdoors. Please come prepared to walk on gentle, yet uneven terrain, and dress appropriately for the weather. 
Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.
