title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Oct 23rd Queer Platonic Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
**[REGISTER HERE](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/oct-23rd-queer-platonic-cuddle)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/oct-23rd-queer-platonic-cuddle)(rsvp's on Meetup do not count as registering)
This is an event for Adults who identify as LGBTQIA+.
The intention of this event is to build community and provide a supportive place for participants to explore sweet platonic physical touch.
No one turned away for lack of funds (please ask if you truly need a scholarship or work trade).
**This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch.** We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

Consent and respect are at the forefront of the experience. We strive for a safe and welcoming environment, fostering a sense of trust that allows attendees to fully enjoy shared touch without any pressure or expectations.

Discover the joy of shared vulnerability in an environment where your authenticity is not just accepted but celebrated. This event is an opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals who appreciate the simplicity of human touch and the profound impact it can have on our well-being.

Express yourself in a way that feels true to you, whether through cozy attire or a touch of personal flair. We encourage individuality and self-expression, creating an inclusive space where everyone can be their authentic selves. Dress code is Casual and cozy.

This is an inclusive environment where we will aim to foster the dismantling of and no tolerance of ableism, fat-shaming, homophobia/transphobia, sexism, xenophobia, classism, racism & other ideas that lead to folks feeling disconnected or unwelcome.

**THE RULES**
1\. Pants stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must ask permission and receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\. Please be specific in your requests\.
4\. If you feel a yes\, say YES\. If you feel a no\, say NO\. If you’re a maybe\, say NO\. You can always change your mind\.
5\. Get your facilitator if you have a question or concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. Talking\, laughter\, silence\, silliness\, stillness\, and crying are welcome\.

**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle.
* Please be free of strong scents; many folks would rather not be close to someone who smells of perfume, essential oils, or cigarettes
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share. The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

We take individual and group safety seriously! if you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at a touch based event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Adult Studio: Introduction to Papermaking
location: NC
description:
This workshop will give you hands-on experience working with several pulps to learn the basics of Western style mould and deckle papermaking. 
Join us to learn: 

how to process recycled and commercial fibers into pulp at home or in a paper studio.
what tools and equipment are needed for papermaking.
how to pull, press and dry sheets of paper.

The day will start with a discussion about papermaking and will explore a variety of handmade paper samples. Afterwards, we will set up vats of pulp and make sheets of paper together. Each participant will take home a stack of sample papers. It’s up to you how you use the finished sheets. All are welcome. No experience necessary. 
ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST
Alyssa Sacora (she/her) is a crafts person working in plant-based mediums of papermaking, book arts, basketry, and weaving. She finds inspiration by observing relationships between plants and humans throughout time. To reduce her footprint and encourage creative thinking, she primarily works with locally available and repurposed natural materials. In addition to and in support of her craft, she tends a large garden in Fairview, North Carolina with fruits and vegetables, medicinal herbs, and art plants. 
Alyssa has taught for a variety of organizations in Western North Carolina and often utilizes an outside setting to help her students make the connection that we are nature and that our lives are intertwined with the plants, the soil, and the air around us. To learn more about Alyssa, see her work and course offerings, visit www.thepatchworkunderground.com.

Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.

description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
How to Overcome Anger with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind.

title: Exhibition on Screen | The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Hieronymus Bosch – Visions of Genius at the Het Noordbrabants Museum (February 13–May 8, 2016) was the largest ever Bosch retrospective, bringing 36 of his 44 surviving works together in Den Bosch. The exhibition took a radical approach, offering research and conservation expertise in exchange for loans from the world’s best museums. Over 420,000 people flocked to the exhibition to marvel at Bosch’s curious creations, with opening hours extended to 1am to accommodate the phenomenal demand. 
Accompanied by expert insights from the exhibition’s curators and leading cultural critics, the film delves into the life of the visionary artist to explore the inspiration behind his strange and haunting works. Contributors include maverick filmmaker and artist Peter Greenaway, The Times’ Chief Art Critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston, and Director of the Het Noordbrabants Museum Dr. Charles de Mooij. 
The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch allows audiences to appreciate the detail of Bosch’s paintings like never before, offering close-up views of the curiosities hidden within his brimming canvases, from cannibalistic clergymen to three- headed birds.

title: Great Smoky Mountains Railroad ~ Fall Excursion 🍂🚂🍁 (SOLD OUT!)
description:
Senior Singles Fun Bunch
Autumn is still quite a long ways off, but if you want to go on this railroad trip you should sign up now and book your seat with Globe Treks! They are only having 14 seats available (open to us and the public) and I’m sure they will fill up fast for this is a very popular day tour!
And a big thanks to both Gaby & Dawn for suggesting this great day tour! Now come join us!

The Great Smokey Railroad day trip is a Nantahala Gorge excursion where we would be on a steam-powered train riding in the crown class. We will also have lunch on the train. Fun!! 🤩

There is just too much to tell you to put in this description section on Meetup. Therefore, please go to Globetreks.com and click on Day Tours. You should see the Great Smoky Mountains Railroad. A full description of what the trip entails will be there with the price, etc. By the way, the price is $299 per person, but so worth it! Only a deposit will be required at this time.

IMPORTANT;
if you decide to go (and I hope you do!) please RSVP on this meetup event after you have booked your seat with Globe Treks. To do this please call Robin (booking agent) at Globe Treks. (828)692-1399. * **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall
location: Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St., Asheville, NC 28801
description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.

Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...

This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

description:

Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?\*\*
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

\*6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle

* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
\*8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
\*11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision.](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.

title: Charming Disaster
description:
Brooklyn-based musical duo Charming Disaster was formed in 2012 by Ellia Bisker and Jeff Morris. Inspired by the gothic humor of Edward Gorey and Tim Burton, the murder ballads of the Americana tradition, and the dramatic flair of the cabaret, they write songs that tell stories, using two voices to explore dark narratives and characters with a playfully macabre sensibility. 



In their interactive Musical Oracle show, songs are selected by chance by audience members who draw cards from the Charming Disaster Oracle Deck—a Tarot-style divination that straddles the line between concert and theatre. 



Charming Disaster has released seven critically acclaimed albums: Love, Crime & Other Trouble (2015), Cautionary Tales (2017), SPELLS + RITUALS (2019), Our Lady of Radium (2022), Super Natural History (2023), singles collection Time Ghost (2024), and The Double (2025). In their songs, the duo have explored love, death, crime, folklore, mythology, magic, science, and the occult. Their theatrical live performances combine vocal harmonies and clever lyrics with ukulele, guitar, and virtuosic foot percussion, drawing listeners into a spooky, offbeat universe of paranormal romance, con artists, circus performers, ancient mythology, nightclubs, car chases, the afterlife, and beyond. 



Charming Disaster’s music has been featured on the podcast Welcome to Night Vale, they have opened for legendary cello-rock ensemble Rasputina, goth icon Voltaire, and punk cabaret duo The Dresden Dolls, and their theatrical, entertaining live performances have captivated audiences across the United States and Europe. They have played festivals, bars and clubs, museums and art galleries, bookstores and libraries, and the occasional historic cemetery. They have appeared alongside storytellers, comedians, fire eaters, puppets, burlesque artists, poets, and circus performers. Recent appearances include the Meadowlark Festival, the Rochester Fringe Festival, Dragon Con, Joe’s Pub at The Public Theater in NYC, Brooklyn’s historic Green-Wood Cemetery, Philadelphia’s Science History Institute, the Edgar Allan Poe Museum in Richmond, VA, Cleveland’s Wizbang Theatre, and the Coney Island Sideshow stage.Music 8:30-11:30pm, $10 cover at the door.

title: The Art of Sound Healing
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
We welcome you to Asheville Art Museum to embrace the fullness of the fall season, to turn inward, root into stillness, and shed what no longer serves us. This morning sanctuary at the Museum offers space to rest, quiet the mind, and dream new intentions into existence. We will use breathwork, meditation, and a 50-minute sound bath to let go of old habits, attachments, and grief, and to drop deep into a state of profound, restorative rest. 
Sound baths promote deep release and relaxation, entraining our brainwaves to shift into a dreamlike state. This gentle, grounding practice is open to everybody—no experience needed. Come as you are, tired or wired, or somewhere in between. Please bring a yoga mat or pad, along with anything else to make you comfortable, like cushions and blankets. 
About the Instructor
Timothy Burgin is a world music percussionist who has spent more than 20 years collecting and playing sound healing instruments. A Kripalu & Pranakriya-trained yoga instructor who has lived and taught in Asheville since 2004, he has completed more than 500 hours of yoga training and founded YogaBasics.com. He leads sound baths throughout Asheville, drawing on his training in acupuncture, bodywork, yoga energetics, anatomy, and physiology. 
Register Now 
What are the Benefits to Sound Bowl Healing Music?
Sound bowl healing music involves the use of crystal or Tibetan singing bowls that produce harmonic vibrations. These vibrations are believed to promote deep relaxation, reduce stress, and support emotional and physical healing. The sound frequencies can help align chakras, calm the nervous system, and create a meditative state conducive to mindfulness and inner peace.

title: A Halloween Walk at the John C. Campbell Folk School in Brasstown NC
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The John C. Campbell Folk School is located in Brasstown, Clay County, NC. It has classes in over 50 subjects, including art, craft, dance, music, and nature. (My wife took lap dulcimer lessons there many years ago. A family friend teaches there regularly.) This is the place where John Jacob Niles first performed a song he had collected, "I Wonder as I Wander".

We will gather in the main parking lot of the campus. Our first stop will be at Keith House, where there are restrooms. We will go to the Craft Shop, follow some trails, visit the Herb Garden, see the Eagle Dancer Sculpture, and past a kiln. This is one walk where we will definitely not hesitate to stop and look at various things there are to see. Your camera is a must on this one.

Our route is 5 KM/3.1 miles. Tennis shoes are fine, as there is no significant elevation change. Most will not want walking sticks (although I plan to take one). Bring a protein snack and plenty of water. Wheelchairs might have a somewhat hard time, but trail strollers should be ok. If I remember, dogs would probably be ok.

Before you leave, you may want to pick up lunch at the Folk School. You might bring a picnic lunch from home. Or you might catch some lunch after you have left campus and are on your way home.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville, NC, who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. title: 5 KM/3 mile Sunday Afternoon Walk in Canton
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The start/finish point is the parking lot for the Rec Park baseball field (not to be confused with the public-school baseball field next to the football stadium—our meeting place is a little further down the road). The field was destroyed by Hurricane Helene, but has been rebuilt, and the parking area is still there. Hopefully, some of the Clyde Elementary School Cardinals Elite Walking Team and their families will be joining us for this event.

We will start our walk at the Canton Recreation Park, go through part of downtown, up Academy Street, past the historic cemetery and the public library, past Pisgah High School, and back to the start point. The up and down are fairly steep.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine. This is all pavement, but some might want walking sticks for the up and down; I plan to walk with a pair of walking sticks. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome.

title: South Arts: Southern Circuit Tour of Independent Filmmakers | They Dream
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for a screening of They Dream followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, William D. Caballero. 
After 20 years of chronicling his Puerto Rican family, a director and his mother craft animations that bring
their loved ones back to life. 
 
Screening time: 1:26:00 
RESERVE TICKETS NOW 
About the filmmaker:
William D. Caballero is an American filmmaker whose work merges documentary, animation, and handcrafted miniature worlds to explore memory, migration, faith, and the emotional architecture of family. Across film, television, and short-form media, Caballero has developed a singular visual language rooted in tactile set-building, intergenerational storytelling, and a deep reverence for his Puerto Rican heritage. In 2001, he was awarded the prestigious Gates Millennium Scholarship, recognizing his academic promise and leadership at an early stage in his career. He went on to earn a BFA from Pratt Institute in 2006 and an
MA from New York University (NYU) in 2008. 
This foundation in both fine art and cinematic storytelling laid the groundwork for a practice that bridges visual art, documentary realism, and experimental fabrication. While at NYU, Caballero created American Dreams Deferred, his first (but not last) autobiographical feature about his family. Caballero first gained widespread recognition in 2015 as the creator of the HBO series Gran’Pa Knows Best, which premiered on HBO and ran for two seasons. Centered on 3D-printed miniature recreations of his Puerto Rican grandfather, the series combined playful scale with emotional depth, redefining what personal storytelling could look like on television. Its inventive approach to memory and intergenerational dialogue positioned Caballero as a bold new voice in hybrid nonfiction storytelling. 
Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit. 
  
Limited capacity—reserve tickets today.

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**November 2026 Selection - *Klara and the Sun* by Kazuo Ishiguro**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/059331817X) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/54120408-klara-and-the-sun)

*Here is the story of Klara, an Artificial Friend with outstanding observational qualities, who, from her place in the store, watches carefully the behavior of those who come in to browse, and of those who pass on the street outside. She remains hopeful that a customer will soon choose her. Klara and the Sun is a thrilling book that offers a look at our changing world through the eyes of an unforgettable narrator, and one that explores the fundamental question: what does it mean to love?*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Beads, Mantras & Deities, Mala-Making Workshop
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
**Mantra means ‘mind protection”.**
*\~Tantric Grounds and Paths, Geshe Kelsang Gyatso*

Making a mala, or rosary of prayer beads is more than just an arts & crafts project. If done mindfully, it is a spiritual practice in itself, and the object we create is also special, becoming more and more blessed as we use it.
Mantra recitation is an essential element of many spiritual practices, as a way of requesting protection, blessings, and attainments. Learn how to make your own mala, as well as some simple mantras to connect with enlightened beings such as Buddha Shakyamuni, Avalokiteshvara, and Tara.
Includes all materials.
Cost $35

title: Walk Biltmore Estate's Deer Park Trail on Bittersweet Chocolate w/Almonds Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Travel past the Biltmore House toward Antler Hill Village. Park in the first available area on the left just past the Lagoon. We will access the Deer Park Trail from there. (I will be monitoring the Comments section of this walk page and also Meetup messages. If you get confused or lost, contact me right away.)

Deer Park Trail goes through the Deer Park (though it isn't near Lioncrest and the other DeerPark facilities). It comes to a T intersection. We will go right to where you can access the Garden Trails. Then we will turn around and go up the hill to the South Terrace of the Biltmore House. From there we will retrace our steps to the start point. It is about 2.5 miles round trip, or so says the map.

I've done this walk in both tennis shoes and in light hiking boots (from a different start point). I'll probably bring walking poles for the hill, though most of the walk won't need them.

Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers would probably work.

PS: It being National Bittersweet Chocolate with Almonds Day, we just might enjoy some at the end of the walk!!

title: The Bush Farmhouse Restaurant ~ Featured on “Diners, Drive-ins and Dives”
description:
Senior Singles Fun Bunch
**The Bush Farmhouse offers South African-inspired food and drink. Their dishes are prepared with fresh produce from their on-site garden and greenhouse.**

**This restaurant caught my eye for it was recently featured in an episode of Guy Fieri’s “Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives” in May 2026. The restaurant is quite unique. They have quaint decor plus a small outdoor menagerie of rescue animals ~ miniature donkeys, ducks, chickens, pigs, etc. 🫏 🐓 🐖 I thought it would be fun to check it out so come join me!**

**MENU:** **www.bushfarmhouse.com**
**They offer vegetarian and vegan options. Also cocktails, beer & wines. 🍹🍺 🍷**

**TABLE RESERVATIONS: 12:30 PM**
**The max number of attendees the restaurant will allow me is 16. So RSVP now!**

**PETS: 🐶** **Allowed on outdoor covered and uncovered patio areas.**

**GIFT-SHOP:** **They carry their own Bush Farmhouse merchandise.**

**PARKING: 🅿️** **On-site parking available.**

**NOTE:** **The restaurant is located only a few blocks (2-minute walk) from downtown Black Mountain so after you eat (or even before) you might want to check out the cool shops.**

**LAKE TOMAHAWK PARK:** **This public park might interest you while you’re in the area. It’s only 1/2 mile from downtown Black Mountain. It’s 16.3 acre and has walking trails, a playground, a fishing pier, and, of course, the 8.9 acre scenic lake.**

**So come join me for lunch at the Bush Farmhouse Restaurant and then go stroll downtown while you’re in the area or go check out Lake Tomahawk!**

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

title: New Moon Ceremony
description:
Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮
Join us for a gathering to set new intentions and connect with the energy of the new moon.
Meet the New Moon in ceremony through astrology, Akashic soul journeying, ritual & embodied intention.
Approaching the threshold of a new lunar cycle with intentionality is a powerful choice that becomes even more amplified when done in community.

The New Moon offers a monthly portal to pause, listen inward, and consciously seed what you desire to cultivate in the cycle ahead. Gathering in ceremony creates the space to step outside the momentum of everyday life and meet that threshold with presence, allowing your intentions to be witnessed, embodied, and amplified within the collective.

Each New Moon also carries the unique energetic signature of the zodiac sign it moves through, offering different themes and invitations for your growth. By working intentionally with the astrology of each lunation, you can align your intentions with the energies already available to you and receive deeper clarity around what is ready to begin.

Each month, we gather at the Soul Sanctuary beneath the dark moon sky for an evening of astrology, soul journeying, ritual, and embodied intention.

**This month with the Scorpio New Moon, we invite you beneath the surface, into the places where truth, power, intimacy, and transformation reside.**

**Together, we’ll work with Scorpio’s alchemical medicine to release what has run its course, reclaim energy or power we’ve given away, and plant intentions rooted in the deeper truth of who we are becoming.**

**What to Expect**

* Guided drop-in meditation
* Astrological teaching + transmission
* Guided Akashic soul journey
* Reflection + intention setting
* Ceremonial fire offerings
* Closing embodiment + integration
* Sacred space for connection and community

No prior experience with astrology, meditation, or ceremonial practice is necessary. Simply come as you are.

**About Your Facilitators**
Alessandra Mary is a trained priestess, ceremonialist, and Akashic guide devoted to creating spaces where the sacred becomes something you can experience, embody, and weave into everyday life.

Jenn is a witch of the cosmos and astrologer who brings the language of the stars down to earth, illuminating the energetic patterns and possibilities available within each lunar cycle.

Together, Alessandra and Jenn weave the mystical and the embodied, the cosmic and the ceremonial, creating a space where you can not only understand the energy of the New Moon, but more importantly, experience it.

**What to Bring**
Our ceremony will primarily take place outside on the grass around the fire, with a large covered porch available as our rain plan. Please dress with the evening weather in mind.

**Be sure to bring:**

* Water bottle
* Journal + pen
* Comfortable clothing and layers appropriate for the weather
* Any sacred objects, crystals, talismans, or other items you would like to place on our collective altar and charge during the ceremony

Lawn blankets and meditation cushions will be provided, though you are very welcome to bring your own blanket, cushion, or camping chair if you’d prefer.

Come ready to slow down, listen deeply, sit beneath the dark moon, and lean into what is waiting to begin.

**PLEASE NOTE: Pre-registration is required for this event to honor the capacity of the space.** If you would like to skip the eventbrite fees, you can Venmo us $30 [here](https://venmo.com/u/iamalessandramary "https://venmo.com/u/iamalessandramary"):

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

### The Lowdown:

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.
* **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur’s Court - Mark Twain
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
**Mark Twain moves from broad comedy to biting social satire in this literary classic.**

**Cracked on the head by a crowbar in nineteenth-century Connecticut, Hank Morgan wakes to find himself in King Arthur’s England. After using his knoweldge of an upcoming solar eclipse to escape a death sentence, Hank must then navigate his way through a medieval world whose idyllic surface masks fear, injustice, and ignorance.**

**Considered by H. L. Mencken to be “the most bitter critic of American platitude and delusion…that ever lived,” Twain enchants readers with a Camelot that strikes disturbingly contemporary notes in this acclaimed tour de force that encompasses both the pure joy of wild high jinks and deeply probing insights into the nature of man.**

description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

"They make a classic bluegrass sound that's not afraid to go somewhere new." —Appalachian Jamwich



Born from the tradition of bluegrass jams & potlucks, THE PLATE SCRAPERS — Derek Kretzer (banjo), Andrew Jordan (guitar), Robbie Mann (fiddle), Jody Mosser (dobro), and Kevin Johnson (bass) — have been putting in the work and showcasing their love for the genre since 2014. They’ve since released 3 studio albums, 3 live albums, and have toured relentlessly up and down the east coast and into the midwest. 



In 2019, they won the Podunk Bluegrass Telefunken Band Contest. They have been featured on WAMU Bluegrass Country Radio, performed as an IBMA Official Showcase artist, and their latest release, "Destination Horizon" (2020) debuted at #9 on the Bluegrass Album Billboard charts with rave reviews from Bluegrass Today. 



As a progressively-minded bluegrass band that strives to maintain a healthy equilibrium between their diverse musical backgrounds and traditional Appalachian sounds, they’ve wowed audiences across the entire spectrum, truly feeling at home on any stage. 



They’ve provided direct support for bluegrass legends such as The Seldom Scene, Frank Solivan & Dirty Kitchen, and Larry Keel. On the other side of that coin, they aren’t afraid to get weird at a late night festival slot and have become well known for their tastefully balanced and refreshingly diverse songwriting. 



Catch their live show and you’ll be sure to receive a full helping of hard-driving bluegrass favorites and heart-wrenching country ballads!Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door.

title: Choose Between a 5 KM/3.1 Mile and a 10 KM/6.2 Mile Guided Waynesville Walk
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We will be joining the Asheville Amblers, AARP, the Cardinals Elite Walking Team, and perhaps some others for this event. Registration is at 9:30 a.m. with step-off at 10:00. The walk is free, although the Amblers do accept donations (suggested donation $4.00).

Meet in front of Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. The walks go past public art, Civil War sites, along the Waynesville Greenway, and more. The 10 KM walk adds Town Hall, the historic Frog Level area, nice neighborhoods, and a peaceful cemetery with spectacular views.

Note: the 5 KM walk will be at a slightly slower pace. The 10 KM walk will be at a slightly faster pace.

There are some hills, so some may want walking poles (I will be taking both of mine); sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok, though it will require one or two work-arounds. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather.

Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it.

Many people go out to eat together after this walk at places like Sweet Onion and Angelos. You will want to shop at Mast General Store and several other downtown shops. The last time we did this walk, people were asking about the availability of ice cream and chocolates.

Why not make a day of it!

Asheville Tech Events

Join us for our monthly project/co-working day! Bring your own project for co-working or jump in on an existing project. We can use all different kinds of support, from emailing to data entry to coding.

Hi Wire Brewing - Biltmore Village / Guajiro Cuban food truck
2A Huntsman Pl, Asheville, NC 28803

**What to expect:**
(Feel free to drop in when you can and leave when you need to.)

* *11am*: Arrival and introductions. Say hi and catch up with your Code with Asheville crew.
* *11:15-11:30am*: Folks chat through what they hope to accomplish for the day, ask for help, and divide into small groups for certain projects. This is a great place to get plugged in if you're looking for a project to work on.
* *11:30am*: We get to work! Some of us stay in the main meeting chat room while we work, others go heads offline.
* 1-2*pm*: Wrap up our work for that day until next time

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

description:

tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
